# Organ and Bone Medications
These repair specific organs, or help bones heal. They work on organs that are damaged or failing; a dead organ needs replacing surgically. See [textlink="Organs" link="CMUGuideMedicalOrgans"].
- [bold]Cardiocaine[/bold]: repairs the heart, and can sometimes restart a heart that has stopped. - [bold]Pulmovine[/bold]: repairs the lungs. - [bold]Hepatocytin[/bold]: repairs the liver. - [bold]Nephronate[/bold]: repairs the kidneys. - [bold]Alkysine[/bold]: repairs the brain. - [bold]Imidazoline[/bold]: repairs the eyes. - [bold]OsteoCalc[/bold]: helps broken bones mend and speeds up bone healing. It doesn't replace setting a fracture. See [textlink="Fractures" link="CMUGuideMedicalBones"]. - [bold]Epinephrine[/bold]: a heart and muscle stimulant, useful for restarting the heart. It also stops allergic reactions and dulls pain. Overdose at 10.5 units, which stresses the heart.
Most organ medicines overdose at 25 units.
